text:
ashwin: Hey @katie @procurement-bot, CostSight renewal quote just landed. Contract ends 2026-04-20, they sent a new rate card that mixes token tier + compute-hour SKUs. Can we quick-check gap vs current usage? :eyes:

katie: sending current usage snapshot in a sec. Are we open to a 12mo commit? We have Dedicated customers coming up, so predict ~2x embeddings next qtr.

procurement-bot: vendor_renewal: CostSight contract CS-2023-77 exp 2026-04-20 — automated reminder (28 days to renew).

vendor_julia (CostSight): Hi all — thanks for the ping. Attached is a simplified rate card. PAYG: embeddings $0.0009 per vector, tokens $0.0007 per 1k tokens. 12mo commit tiers: 10% off @ $50k/yr, 20% off @ $100k/yr. Commits include SSO + 24/7 support.

ashwin: can you clarify embeddings SKU — is that per vector vs per 1k vectors? The quote says 'per call' which is ambiguous.

vendor_julia (CostSight): Sorry for shorthand — embeddings = per vector. If you batch we can meter per-batch or convert to per-1k-vectors on the invoice. We can tweak wording in the SOW.

katie: here's quick usage snapshot:
```
month: feb-2026
embeddings_vectors: 2,100,000
tokens: 45,000,000
avg_embedding_batch: 16
```
Can you run a simple est for PAYG vs 12mo 20% commit?

vendor_julia (CostSight): Quick calc:
PAYG embeddings = 2.1M * $0.0009 = $1,890
PAYG tokens = 45M / 1000 * $0.0007 = $31.50
=> Total PAYG ≈ $1,921.50 per month (~$23k/yr)
20% commit (naive) => ~$1,537/month (~$18.4k/yr)
Note: commits have a minimum invoice floor (example: $40k/yr). Commits only make sense if annualized usage >= floor.

ashwin: that floor is the kicker. Our annualized PAYG (~$23k) is below their $40k floor — not ideal.

katie: ok we should push on floor or ask for an escalator: start at $30k floor with a 6mo true-up. Also request metering to be per-1k vectors for billing clarity.

ashwin: vendor_julia, can you do a smaller commit or a pilot with credits + support? We can trade a 9mo partial commit for a lower floor.

vendor_julia (CostSight): We can offer a 9mo pilot: $30k floor, 10% discount, and monthly true-up. Support tier stays standard. I'll draft a short addendum and send redlines.

procurement-bot: Suggested next step: request SOW/addendum and vendor redlines. Approvers: @katie, @samir-finance, @ashwin. Start procurement workflow: `/procure start` when ready.

samir-finance: +1. Need a short TCO: current PAYG vs pilot. If pilot reduces unit cost but adds floor, show cashflow and break-even date.

ashwin: I'll draft a 1-pager TCO and share in this thread. vendor_julia, can you add sample invoice lines with per-1k-vector metering and the proposed true-up clause?

vendor_julia (CostSight): Will send sample invoice lines and a redline by EOD. Happy to hop on a 15min call if helpful.

katie: thanks everyone. @ashwin once you post the TCO let's move to `/procure start` and loop legal.
